data.title: Corn basis steady-higher, soy basis steady-lower
data.description:
Basis bids for soybeans were steady to lower in the US Midwest on Friday, while corn basis bids were flat to higher, dealers said.

  • Dealers have been trying to incentivize farmers to sell their crops this week, as US futures prices have been under pressure and the completion of the harvest has kept producers busy.

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported on Friday that exporters sold 100,000 metric tons of soymeal to Spain for delivery in the 2026/27 marketing year.

  • Deforestation rules going into effect in the European Union in late December could steer soymeal export demand toward US supplies and, in turn, create more domestic demand for the oilseed in the US, analysts said.

  • CBOT January soybeans settled up 13-1/4 cents at $12.20-3/4 per bushel, bolstered by fresh export demand for soymeal and expectations of tightening US soybean inventories.

  • CBOT December corn ended down 4-1/2 cents at $4.34-1/2 per bushel, though the benchmark March contract stayed above a 4-1/2-month low set one day earlier.

data.title: TechCreate Group Ltd. Provides Update on NYSE American Delisting Proceedings
data.description:
TechCreate Group Ltd. (OTCMKTS: TCGLF) (“TechCreate” or the “Company”), a technology consultancy and advanced software solutions provider specializing in payment solutions, cybersecurity, and digital services, announced that the NYSE American Committee for Review (the “Committee”) has unanimously determined to affirm the decision of the NYSE American LLC (“NYSE American” or the “Exchange”) Listing Qualifications Panel (the “Panel”) with respect to the delisting of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares. Following its review, the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”) has determined not to pursue any further challenge to the Committee’s decision.

The Committee’s written decision, dated November 9, 2026, follows a hearing held on October 22, 2026 and affirms the Panel’s August 20, 2026 opinion, which upheld the NYSE American Staff (“Staff”) determination to commence delisting proceedings. The proceedings stem from the one-day trading suspension of the Company’s securities ordered by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) and effective on February 2, 2026, the stated basis for which was potential manipulation of the Company’s securities through social media recommendations made by unknown persons.

In reaching its determination, the Board reviewed the sequence of the appeal proceedings and the Committee’s written decision, and considered the following:

  • No finding of wrongdoing. The Committee’s decision states that the Staff’s investigation into the manipulative trading of the Company’s securities did not result in a finding of wrongdoing on the part of the Company or any of its officers and directors.

  • Exchange discretion. The Committee determined that the NYSE American Company Guide (the “Company Guide”) gives the Staff discretion to delist a security regardless of whether the issuer complies with applicable listing standards. The Committee acknowledged the preventive measures the Company put forward, including voluntary surveillance, reporting and escalation procedures, and enhanced Board oversight, but did not consider them sufficient to continue the listing.

  • Focus on the business. The Board believes the Company’s time and resources are better directed to operating and growing the business, and to evaluating alternatives intended to protect the interests of shareholders.

Under Section 1206 of the Company Guide, the Committee’s decision may be called for review by the Exchange’s Board of Directors at the request of one or more of its directors. If the decision is not called for review, the Company will be notified that it represents the final action of the Exchange. If the decision is not called for review and the Company receives such notice, the Exchange is expected to proceed with delisting of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares. The Company’s securities continue to be quoted in the over-the-counter market under the symbol TCGLF.

About TechCreate Group Ltd.

TechCreate Group Ltd. is a Singapore-based payment software solutions provider. Founded in 2015, the Company delivers digital payment and infrastructure solutions to financial institutions, telecommunications companies, deposit insurers and enterprises. TechCreate’s offerings include real-time payment systems, digital banking platforms, API management, cybersecurity and cloud computing. Its proprietary Artificial Intelligence Real-Time Engine (AI-RTE) is designed to enable fast, secure and efficient payment processing. For more information, visit https://www.techcreate.com.sg/.

data.title: Ironman Announces Amendment to Convertible Debentures
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

LANGLEY, BC, November 20, 2026 – TheNewswire – Ironman International Ltd. (TSXV: IMI) (OTCQB: IMITF) ("Ironman" or the "Company") announces that it is seeking TSX Venture Exchange ("TSXV") acceptance for an extension of the maturity date and a reduction of the conversion price of the aggregate $500,000 principal amount of the secured convertible debentures ("Debentures") that were originally issued on November 22, 2022.

The Debentures are convertible into common shares of the Company (“Shares”) and mature on November 22, 2026. The Company is seeking approval of the TSXV to amend the Debentures (the “Replacement Debentures”) on maturity to reduce the conversion price of the Debentures from $0.10 to $0.05 per Share and extend the maturity date to November 30, 2026. The Debentures bear interest at a rate of 12.0% per annum, which has been paid in cash by the Company on a monthly basis. The Debentures have a remaining principal amount of an aggregate of $500,000.

The issuance of the Replacement Debentures remains subject to TSXV acceptance. The Company will issue a subsequent news release upon receipt of TSXV acceptance.

Related Party Transaction

Debentures having a principal amount of $225,000 are held by 599837 B.C. Ltd. (“599”), a company owned and controlled by Mike Irmen, director of the Company, and Debentures having a principal amount of $25,000 are held by Robert Scott, a director of the Company. As such, the Replacement Debentures issued to 599 and Mr. Scott will constitute a “related party transaction” pursuant to Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions (“MI 61-101”). The Company has relied on the exemptions from the valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements of MI 61-101 contained in sections 5.5(a) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 on the basis that the Debentures do not exceed 25% of the fair market value of the Company’s market capitalization.

About Ironman International Ltd.

Established in 1999, Ironman International Ltd. is a leading North American provider of horizontal directional drilling and trenchless infrastructure services, operating 24/7 to support residential, commercial, industrial, and utility clients. The Company specializes in delivering cost-effective, low-impact underground installation solutions across a broad range of applications, including telecommunications, electrical, water and sewer, oil and gas, geothermal, and irrigation systems. With a modern fleet of specialized equipment and an experienced technical team, Ironman is capable of executing complex projects across diverse and challenging environments, including lakes, rivers, coastal and near-shore marine installations, rail corridors, roadways, and highways. The Company also provides complementary services designed to enhance efficiency, maintain safety standards, and ensure projects are completed on time and on budget. The common shares of Ironman International Ltd. are listed on the TSX Venture Exchange and trade under the symbol “IMI” and trade on the OTCQB Venture Market under the symbol “IMITF”.

data.title: Fitch Affirms Belgium's Credit Rating, Warns of High Debt Levels
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Fitch Ratings affirmed Belgium's credit rating and outlook while warning that the country's strengths are somewhat offset by its high levels of debt and political environment.

The credit ratings firm assigned Belgium an A+ sovereign debt rating and a stable outlook due to its diversified and wealthy economy, as well as its membership in the eurozone.

Belgium's public debt is rising and is among the highest in the A rating category, Fitch said. Debt is set to be nearly 110% of gross domestic product by the end of this year, compared with the A rating average of 60%.

The nation's deficit is expected to start rising again in 2029 due to income tax reduction and a further rise in debt interest expenses.

Belgium's structural reforms implemented this year and last should contain social spending, Fitch said. However, fiscal pressure from rising costs persist and the reform measures have sparked protests.

Growth in the country was weaker in the first half of this year than expected, causing Fitch to lower its growth forecast for the year to 0.7%. Private consumption has suffered from higher energy prices, while exports are starting to recover after years of underperformance.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Lutnick asked battery startup Pure Lithium to accept US takeover, documents and source say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Lutnick sought majority control of battery startup in July
  • Pure Lithium's batteries seen as appealing by US government
  • Startup rejected request, offered 9.9% stake instead that was rebuffed

By Ernest Scheyder

US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asked battery startup Pure Lithium in July to give Washington a 51% controlling stake in exchange for funds to build a manufacturing plant that the company would not own or control, according to documents reviewed by Reuters and a person with direct knowledge of the request.

The company rejected the proposal, saying such a stake would likely garner public scrutiny, risk future capital-raising and outweigh any benefit to shareholders, the documents from July and August showed.

"51% is far outside precedent and invites scrutiny," Pure Lithium's legal counsel Skadden Arps wrote in an August 22 memorandum reviewed by Reuters that outlined Lutnick's request.

The federal government's unsuccessful attempt to take majority control of Pure Lithium has not been previously reported.

This article is based on documents that include emails between Pure Lithium and the Commerce Department discussing a meeting between Lutnick and Pure Lithium's CEO, as well as a memorandum written by Pure Lithium's legal counsel outlining Lutnick's request.

Lutnick's plan marks one of the latest moves by the Trump administration to acquire a stake in an American company and comes as the secretary and former investment banker faces increased scrutiny over his ties to corporate executives and companies affected by decisions made by his department.

The Trump administration has taken stakes in several companies since Donald Trump returned to the White House, including chipmaker Intel , extending its reach into the private sector in a way recent administrations have not.

However, it has not taken a majority stake in any company, with its most serious effort a proposed rescue of Spirit Airlines, the low-budget airline that ceased operations in May. Thus far, the largest equity stake the Trump administration has agreed to would give it a 15% stake in rare earths company MP Materials , which would make it the largest shareholder.

A Pure Lithium representative, when asked about the proposal, did not dispute the account.

The Commerce Department did not respond to questions about the proposal posed by Reuters for this story.

It is not illegal for the federal government to acquire equity stakes in a private company and the administration has defended these efforts, particularly through using funds stemming from 2022's CHIPS Act, which was designed to boost domestic research and manufacturing of semiconductors.

Lawmakers opposed to the practice, though, contend the law never authorized such ownership. No court has ruled on the question.

Privately held Pure Lithium has developed a lithium metal battery that it says is far more efficient than a traditional lithium-ion battery and can be built without graphite, nickel or cobalt.

If Pure Lithium's battery can deliver, it would be a major advancement for the energy storage industry. If mass produced, the battery could potentially shift how the US military and other federal contractors power millions of devices, analysts have said.

At a July 29 meeting in Washington with Pure Lithium CEO Emilie Bodoin, Lutnick expressed interest in the battery's capabilities, including its efficiency. He said the US government needed to control the company so the battery could be used by the US military and other agencies, according to the person and documents reviewed by Reuters.

The two had been meeting to discuss a legal dispute with Japan's Panasonic related to the battery technology, according to the person and the documents.

The meeting, which lasted roughly 45 minutes, was arranged by billionaire Robert Friedland, one of Pure Lithium's largest shareholders. A company co-founded by Friedland, I-Pulse, received $250 million from the Commerce Department in June.

Friedland attended the July meeting alongside David Shapiro, a senior adviser at the Commerce Department, according to the documents. Through a spokesperson, Friedland declined to comment for this article.

The White House has repeatedly said strategic investments in the minerals and related sectors are needed because they are critical to US economic competitiveness. The White House did not respond to requests for comment for this article.

Reuters has no evidence that Lutnick personally holds a stake in either I-Pulse or Pure Lithium. A Commerce Department spokesperson, speaking on behalf of Lutnick, said she did not think he is invested in either company. Both companies are privately held and do not need to disclose their ownership.

US CONTROL DISCUSSED

As part of his effort to persuade Bodoin to give the government the controlling stake, Lutnick said the takeover could also help with the Panasonic dispute, according to the person. Pure Lithium sued Panasonic in March, accusing the Japanese company of reverse-engineering Pure Lithium's lithium metal battery technology, an allegation Panasonic disputes. The case is set for a January hearing to decide whether to grant Pure Lithium a preliminary injunction against Panasonic.

The Commerce chief had previously helped negotiate a tariff-linked agreement last year that included a $550 billion pledge from Tokyo to invest in the US economy.

In exchange for the majority stake, Lutnick said that $1 billion from Japan's pledge would be set aside to build a manufacturing plant that a special-purpose investment vehicle controlled by Tokyo and Washington would own, according to an August 22 memo from Pure Lithium's attorneys to Friedland.

However, Pure Lithium would not have received any funding under the proposal, according to the documents. The company would have been contracted to operate but not own the plant, and would be granted a portion of the plant's revenue after paying for the debt servicing costs on the invested $1 billion.

Lutnick also told Pure Lithium to send 100 of its batteries to the Energy and Defense departments for testing, according to the documents.

Pure Lithium rejected Lutnick's requests, citing the lack of funds in the proposal for the company and expected public scrutiny, saying such an arrangement would "cripple Pure Lithium's ability to raise capital or pursue an IPO," according to the memorandum written by Pure Lithium's counsel Skadden Arps, which objected because Pure Lithium would not have control of the proposed manufacturing plant.

The Commerce Department rejected Pure Lithium's 9.9% counterproposal in August.

"Commerce remains fixed on 51% equity in Pure Lithium," said the August 22 memo from Pure Lithium's attorneys to Friedland. The Commerce Department "is prepared to move on to other projects if Pure Lithium does not meet the mark."

Lutnick has boosted the Commerce Department's investments in the minerals sector as part of a plan first reported by Reuters last year to reallocate funding approved in the 2022 CHIPS Act for semiconductor research and factory construction.

Those interests include stakes in USA Rare Earth and Korea Zinc , while other federal agencies have taken stakes in different mining companies.

data.title: Surgery Partners, Inc. Announces Expiration and Results of Consent Solicitation Relating to Surgery Center Holdings, Inc.’s 7.250% Senior Notes due 2032
data.description:
BRENTWOOD, Tenn., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Surgery Partners, Inc. (“Surgery Partners”) announced today the results of the previously announced solicitation of consents (the “Consent Solicitation”) by its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Surgery Center Holdings, Inc. (the “Issuer”), from holders (“Holders”) of its outstanding $1,225,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 7.250% Senior Notes due 2032 (CUSIP Nos. 86881W AF9 / U86786 AD9 / U86786 AE7; ISINs US86881WAF95 / USU86786AD98 / USU86786AE71) (the “Notes”) to certain proposed amendments (the “Proposed Amendments”) to the indenture governing the Notes, dated as of April 10, 2024 (as supplemented, the “Indenture”), among the Issuer, the guarantors party thereto and Wilmington Trust, National Association, as trustee (the “Trustee”). The Consent Solicitation was made upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Issuer’s Consent Solicitation Statement, dated November 16, 2026 (as amended by Amendment No. 1 thereto, dated November 16, 2026, and Amendment No. 2 thereto, dated November 18, 2026, the “Consent Solicitation Statement”).

The Consent Solicitation expired at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 20, 2026 (the “Expiration Time”). As of the Expiration Time, according to information provided by S&P Global Inc., the information and tabulation agent for the Consent Solicitation, the Issuer had received the requisite consents with respect to the Notes (the “Requisite Consents”) to effect the Proposed Amendments.

As previously announced, on October 23, 2026, Surgery Partners entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (as amended by Amendment No. 1 thereto, dated as of November 8, 2026, and as it may be further amended, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Merger Agreement”) with Spyglass Topco, LLC (“Topco”), Spyglass Merger Subsidiary, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Topco (“Merger Sub”), and, solely for the limited purposes set forth therein, Bon Secours Mercy Health, Inc. (“BSMH”). Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub will merge with and into Surgery Partners, with Surgery Partners surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Topco (the “Merger”).

The Proposed Amendments will amend the Indenture to (i) provide that, concurrently with and following the consummation of the Merger in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement on or prior to the date that is five business days after the End Date (as defined in the Merger Agreement), each of BSMH, HealthSpan Partners, a 501(c)(3) Ohio corporation affiliated with BSMH, and their respective affiliates, and certain groups of which any of them are members, will be “Permitted Holders” under the Indenture, in addition to the existing Permitted Holders, and (ii) add to, amend, supplement or change certain other defined terms in the Indenture related to the foregoing. Except for the Proposed Amendments, all existing terms of the Notes and the Indenture will remain unchanged, and the Proposed Amendments will not alter the Issuer’s obligation to pay the principal of or interest on the Notes or the stated interest rate or maturity date of the Notes.

The Issuer intends to execute a supplemental indenture to the Indenture setting forth the Proposed Amendments (the “Supplemental Indenture”) on or around November 24, 2026. The Supplemental Indenture will become effective upon its execution and delivery, but the Proposed Amendments will become operative only immediately prior to the consummation of the Merger, provided that the Consent Fee has been paid. Once operative, the Proposed Amendments will be binding on all Holders, including those that did not deliver consents. If the Consent Fee is paid but the Merger is not consummated on or prior to the date that is five business days after the End Date, the Proposed Amendments will not become operative, and Holders that received the Consent Fee will retain it.

Holders who validly delivered (and did not validly revoke) consents prior to the Expiration Time will receive a cash payment equal to $5.00 per $1,000 in principal amount of Notes for which such consents were delivered (the “Consent Fee”). The Issuer expects to pay the Consent Fee on November 24, 2026, whether or not the Merger is consummated.

Jefferies LLC acted as solicitation agent and S&P Global Inc. acted as information and tabulation agent in connection with the Consent Solicitation. Questions regarding the Consent Solicitation may be directed to Jefferies LLC at (212) 284-2368 (collect) or to S&P Global Inc. at (212) 849-3880 (banks and brokers) or (888) 593-9546 (toll-free), or by email at consentoffer@spglobal.com.

This press release is for informational purposes only and does not constitute an offer to purchase or a solicitation of an offer to sell the Notes or any other securities and does not constitute a solicitation of consents with respect to the Notes or any other securities. The Consent Solicitation was made only by, and pursuant to the terms of, the Consent Solicitation Statement, and the information in this press release is qualified in its entirety by reference to the Consent Solicitation Statement.

About Surgery Partners

Surgery Partners is a leading healthcare services company with a differentiated outpatient delivery model focused on providing high quality, cost effective solutions for surgical and related ancillary care in support of both patients and physicians. Founded in 2004, Surgery Partners is one of the largest and fastest growing surgical services businesses in the country, with more than 200 locations in 30 states, including ambulatory surgery centers, surgical hospitals, multi-specialty physician practices and urgent care facilities.

Additional Information and Where to Find It

In connection with the proposed acquisition by an affiliate of BSMH of the Company (the “Transactions”), the Company will file with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) a proxy statement (the “Proxy Statement”), a definitive version of which will be mailed or otherwise provided to its stockholders. The Company and certain other filing persons intend to jointly file a transaction statement on Schedule 13E-3 (the “Schedule 13E-3”). The Company may also file other documents with the SEC regarding the proposed Transactions. BEFORE MAKING ANY VOTING DECISION, THE COMPANY’S STOCKHOLDERS ARE URGED TO CAREFULLY READ THE PROXY STATEMENT AND THE SCHEDULE 13E-3 IN THEIR ENTIRETY WHEN THEY BECOME AVAILABLE AND ANY OTHER DOCUMENTS FILED WITH THE SEC AS WELL AS ANY AMENDMENTS OR SUPPLEMENTS THERETO IN CONNECTION WITH THE PROPOSED TRANSACTIONS OR INCORPORATED BY REFERENCE THEREIN BECAUSE THEY WILL CONTAIN IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT THE PROPOSED TRANSACTIONS AND THE PARTIES TO THE PROPOSED TRANSACTIONS. Investors and security holders may obtain free copies of the Proxy Statement, the Schedule 13E-3 and other documents that the Company files with the SEC (when available) from the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov and the Company’s website at ir.surgerypartners.com. In addition, the Proxy Statement, the Schedule 13E-3 and other documents filed by the Company with the SEC (when available) may be obtained from the Company free of charge by directing a request to the Company’s Investor Relations at IR@surgerypartners.com.

Participants in the Solicitation

The Company and certain of its directors, executive officers and employees may be deemed to be participants in the solicitation of proxies from the Company’s stockholders in connection with the proposed Transactions. Information regarding the persons who may, under the rules of the SEC, be deemed to be participants in the solicitation of the stockholders of the Company in connection with the proposed Transactions, including a description of their respective direct or indirect interests, by security holdings or otherwise will be set forth in the Proxy Statement and Schedule 13E-3 and other materials to be filed with the SEC. You may also find additional information about the Company’s directors and executive officers in the Company’s proxy statement for its 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, which was filed with the SEC on April 23, 2026 (the “Annual Meeting Proxy Statement”) , including under the sections entitled “Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management”, “Proposal No. 1 Election of Directors”, and “Executive Officers” therein. To the extent holdings of securities by potential participants (or the identity of such participants) have changed since the information printed in the Annual Meeting Proxy Statement, such information has been or will be reflected in the Company’s Statements of Change in Ownership on Forms 4 filed with the SEC. The Company’s stockholders may obtain additional information regarding the direct and indirect interests of the participants in the solicitation of proxies in connection with the proposed Transactions, including the interests of the Company’s directors and executive officers in the proposed Transactions, which may be different than those of the Company’s stockholders generally, by reading the Proxy Statement and Schedule 13E-3 and other relevant materials to be filed with the SEC relating to the proposed Transactions. You can obtain free copies of these documents from the Company using the contact information above.

No Offer

No person has commenced soliciting proxies in connection with the proposed Transactions referenced in this communication, and this communication is neither an offer to purchase nor a solicitation of an offer to sell securities, nor a solicitation of any vote or approval.

data.title: Gold, silver end worst week in eight months but some analysts see signs of a bottom
data.description:
Gold's rout continued Friday ‌as the metal wrapped up its largest weekly loss in eight months, with the strong dollar, expectations of interest rate increases from the U.S. Federal Reserve, and the selloff in AI-linked stocks continuing to weigh broadly on commodities.

Stock markets fell around the world on Friday after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore faith in the AI trade, ​with investors cutting exposure and apparently taking profits ahead of the end of the year.

Gold's sharp slide has been exacerbated by comments from Fed policymakers that echoed hawkish tones in the FOMC's October meeting, with Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson the latest official to flag inflation risks that ​could warrant another rate hike.

Markets now see a 96% chance of a 25-bp U.S. rate hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch tool.

Central bank buying should provide some support, but the pressure on precious metals could extend into next year until the market sees where the Fed ends up on interest rates, Everbank's president of world markets Chris Gaffney said.

"I'm not looking for that change anytime soon," possibly next year's Q1 or Q2, Gaffney said. "But once they say OK, I think we're good, I think that may be the start of the next leg up for gold."

Gold's failure to attract safe-haven demand during the equity market selloff suggests investors are selling liquid assets to cover losses and reduce risk, Saxo Bank's head of commodity strategy Ole Hansen said in a note.

However, holdings in gold ETFs have remained broadly unchanged over the past month despite the decline in prices, indicating longer-term investors have largely maintained their exposure, Hansen said, adding that gold's "best chance of a rebound may simply be that the selling has become excessive."

"Bond yields have eased somewhat, and the U.S. dollar has stabilized, [so] there is no obvious explanation for the continued and even accelerating decline in the gold price. Renewed forced selling may be playing a role following another selloff in technology stocks," Commerzbank analyst Carsten Fritsch said in a note.

The selling pressure on gold appears increasingly exaggerated, particularly as interest rate expectations have changed little in recent days, Fritsch added.

The U.S. dollar, which continues to trade near a 19-month high, remains a significant headwind for precious metals, Trade Nation senior market analyst David Morrison said, but any pullback in the dollar could provide gold and silver with some much-needed breathing room to stabilize.

On Friday, front-month Comex gold for November delivery dipped 4.6% to $3,512.30/oz, its lowest settlement value since August 29, 2025, and front-month Comex November silver sank 7.4% to $41.035/oz, the lowest close since September 9, 2025.

For the full week, gold and silver sank 9.5% and 16.3%, respectively, with both metals recording their largest one-week declines since the week ending March 20.

data.title: U.K. Debt Will Keep Climbing, Moody's Says — Market Talk
data.description: The U.K. is narrowing its deficit, but that isn't enough to reverse its rising debt, Moody's Ratings says. The rating agency expects the U.K. will narrow its deficit, which reached 5.3% of GDP in 2025, to 4.5% in 2026 and 4% in 2027. The U.K.'s budget for 2027 also confirms its government's commitment to reducing the country's deficit, Moody's says. However, Moody's still expects government debt will grow to 106% of GDP by the end of the decade. Interest rates are expected to stay high relative to revenue. The long average maturity of government debt and deep domestic capital markets limit refinancing and liquidity risks, as well, Moody's says. (katherine.hamilton@wsj.com)
